genZNote: Bullet-shaped, nearly always fatal once symptoms start — which is exactly why post-exposure prophylaxis has to happen before that point.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Central nervous system and salivary glands of infected mammals
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — infects a wide range of mammals; bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes are important reservoirs in different regions; dogs are the main source of human cases globally
habitat.reservoir: Wild and domestic mammals (species vary by region)

identificationClues: Negri bodies — characteristic cytoplasmic inclusions in infected neurons — are a classic (though not always present or practical) histopathologic finding
Direct fluorescent antibody testing of brain tissue (post-mortem) or PCR/antibody testing of saliva, serum, and CSF are current diagnostic methods
History of an animal bite, particularly from a bat, raccoon, skunk, fox, or unvaccinated dog in an endemic area, is the essential clinical clue
Nearly universally fatal once symptoms begin, making prompt post-exposure prophylaxis after a suspected exposure critical

diseases: Rabies — an acute, progressive encephalomyelitis that is nearly always fatal once clinical symptoms appear
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite (or less commonly scratch/mucous membrane exposure to saliva) of an infected mammal
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Dog bites are the source of the large majority of human rabies deaths globally, concentrated in parts of Asia and Africa; in the United States and other countries with canine rabies control, bat exposures are now a leading source of human cases
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Because confirmatory testing (direct fluorescent antibody on brain tissue) is typically only definitive post-mortem, post-exposure prophylaxis decisions are made clinically and epidemiologically, not by waiting for a lab result

examFacts.importantTest: Direct fluorescent antibody test on brain tissue (post-mortem); PCR/antibody testing of saliva, serum, CSF
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Nearly universally fatal once symptomatic — post-exposure prophylaxis after a bite is the critical clinical intervention
